title: installer: tenant-zone CMK placement + installer-signed-audit-envelopes
author: Evan Zhou
release_notes: Private installer: ensure customer CMKs are provisioned in the tenant's configured zone at install time; add an installer-side signer to produce immutable audit envelopes for on-prem/private deployments. Includes preflight checks and a reversible migration path.
description: Background: customers running private/on-prem deployments requested stronger guarantees that customer-managed keys (CMKs) are provisioned and used only within their configured data zone and that audit events emitted by the installer are tamper-evident for compliance audits. This PR adds installer-side enforcement of CMK placement (zone mapping) and an optional installer audit-envelope signer that produces a signed, immutable wrapper for audit batches so customers can retain a verifiable trail outside the control plane. Scope: - Preflight and onboarding validation for tenant->zone CMK mapping (installer preflight fails if CMK references a different region/zone) - Terraform + Helm changes to surface a tenant_kms_map var that binds tenant identifiers to allowed KMS zones - Installer KMS affinity controller that ensures API calls for key usage are routed only to allowed endpoints and rejects cross-zone CMK refs - An installer audit-proxy that signs audit batches with a tenant-scoped signing key (optionally backed by the customer's KMS) and writes signed envelopes to the configured audit sink - Migration helper: attempts safe rebind when an existing CMK is in an unexpected zone and emits a migration plan for operators - Feature flag: infra.install.kms_zone_enforce (default ON for new installs; existing installs are opt-in until migration is applied) Checklist: - [x] Preflight failing behavior implemented and unit-tested - [x] Terraform var + docs added - [x] Helm templates and chart values updated - [x] Audit envelope signer implemented with backward-compatible toggle - [x] Migration tool and a dry-run mode - [x] End-to-end smoke that runs in the CI private-installer job - [x] Security review (SEC-88) completed Design notes and motivation: preventing accidental cross-zone CMK usage reduces blast radius for data residency policies and is required by some customers' contractual controls. The signed audit envelopes provide an append-only proof for regulatory auditors without requiring the control plane to be fully trusted; operators can export these signed envelopes to their long-term retention stores. Implementation details: - installer/bin/preflight-check: new checks validate kms mapping and fail fast with suggested remediation commands - installer/terraform/kms_binding.tf: adds tenant_kms_map variable and validation rules; plan shows a migration recommendation if mismatched - helm/templates/kms-binding.yaml: renders Kubernetes secrets/configmaps that bind installer components to the allowed KMS endpoints - installer/cmd/kms-affinity-controller: light-weight controller that enforces runtime usage of mapped endpoints; rejects attempts to use unbound CMKs (returns 403 to caller) - installer/cmd/audit-signer: signs JSON-lines audit batches using PKCS#7 envelopes; verification helper included in installer/bin/verify-audit-envelope - charts/private-installer/values.schema.json: schema bump; new top-level keys under kms and audit documented - tests/ci/kms-affinity-smoke.sh and tests/unit/test_audit_signer.py added - docs/installer/kms-region-pin.md: operator facing doc and migration steps Rollout plan: - Canary: enable feature for a single internal tenant group in staging for 48h - Migration: run migration-tool dry-run across existing installs, notify operators of required action, then apply opt-in flag to migrate - Broad rollout: enable enforcement for new installs only for two weeks, then begin outreach to existing customers with an auto-migration path and operator-run command. Backout: toggling infra.install.kms_zone_enforce=false disables enforcement immediately; audit-signer can be disabled independently. Security considerations: the installer stores only a reference to the tenant signing key by default; signing may be delegated to customer CMKs via the KMS plugin. Access to signing keys is guarded by RBAC and the installer will log all signing operations as part of the audit envelope. Testing: unit tests added for preflight, controller rejection cases, and signer verification. CI: initial run flagged a flaky test that was hardened; final CI passed. Docs: new operator guide and migration playbook. Related: ENG-4012 (installer security hardening), SEC-88 (audit-envelope design).
